newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end up despite TEM rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end up despite TEM rate rise.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed ahead in slow trade, despite a rise in benchmark TEM yields, as investors bet that Congress would soon approve a crucial package of social security reform bills, traders said.
"It looks as though Congress is going to approve the reforms pretty quickly, and that's good for the market," said Inversiones Union trader Hector Perez.
The Chamber of Deputies has said it will remain in permanent session until the bills, which will free-up Venezuela's rigid labor markets, are passed. The bills will then be sent to the Senate.

The bolsa's 19-share index gained 1.26 percent to close at 6,647.91 points, despite a rise of 235 basis points to 20.15 percent in six month Central Bank TEM yields, used as a benchmark for wider interest rates.
However, analysts said U.S. interest rates, left unchanged after the Federal Reserve met Tuesday, had helped the bourse, as had market talk of a possible hike in electricity tariffs.
Utility Electricidad de Caracas led the bolsa up, surging 2.17 percent to end at 530.00 bolivars as a total of 37 million shares traded, worth 3.5 billion bolivars ($7.1 million).
